articles.title: Proof-of-Antiquity: El Consenso que Valora la Edad del Hardware
articles.excerpt: En un mundo donde la escalabilidad y la eficiencia energética dominan las conversaciones sobre blockchain, RustChain introduce una propuesta radicalmente contraintuitiva: Proof-of-Antiquity (PoA). A d…
articles.body: En un mundo donde la escalabilidad y la eficiencia energética dominan las conversaciones sobre blockchain, RustChain introduce una propuesta radicalmente contraintuitiva: Proof-of-Antiquity (PoA) . A diferencia de Proof-of-Work (PoW), que premia la potencia bruta, o Proof-of-Stake (PoS), que favorece la riqueza acumulada, PoA otorga autoridad proporcional a la antigüedad del hardware . No se trata de una curiosidad técnica, sino de una filosofía de gobernanza descentralizada que busca resistir la centralización inducida por la obsolescencia tecnológica. ¿Qué es Proof-of-Antiquity? Proof-of-Antiquity es un mecanismo de consenso diseñado para garantizar que cada unidad de procesamiento —cada CPU— tenga exactamente un voto , independientemente de su velocidad, arquitectura o generación.

articles.title: Access Atlas: keyboard repair plans from structured W3C guidance
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Sanity Challenge, Path One: Ship an Agent That Queries Real Content. Access Atlas is a small keyboard and focus repair agent. Give it a symptom such as “Tab leaves my moda…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Sanity Challenge, Path One: Ship an Agent That Queries Real Content . What I Built Access Atlas is a small keyboard and focus repair agent. Give it a symptom such as “Tab leaves my modal” or “arrowing through tabs loads every slow panel,” and it selects source-linked guidance from Sanity. The product plan brings together the repair steps, prerequisites, constraints, suggested manual checks, expected observations, and original W3C source. The corpus contains seven repair topics. Its boundaries matter: a menu trigger needs an actual ARIA menu; automatic tab activation depends on panel timing; visible focus is a different question from contrast; and Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) does not demand complete component exposure.

articles.title: VMware Tanzu Agent Deployment: Build Packs, MCP Gateways, and Multi-Tenant Security
articles.excerpt: AI agents are crossing the chasm from developer laptops to enterprise infrastructure. When that happens, security boundaries, multi-tenancy, and compliance become non-negotiable. VMware Tanzu Platform…
articles.body: AI agents are crossing the chasm from developer laptops to enterprise infrastructure. When that happens, security boundaries, multi-tenancy, and compliance become non-negotiable. VMware Tanzu Platform is deploying agents alongside traditional applications in production environments, and the plumbing looks different from what you build in a prototype. Nick Kuhn from VMware Tanzu Platform walked through what changes when agents run in enterprise environments: agent build packs, MCP gateways, shared memory coordination, identity management, and sandboxing primitives. This is platform engineering applied to agent workloads. Agent Build Packs vs. Container Build Packs Traditional container build packs package application code, dependencies, and runtime into a deployable artifact.

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend . FriendFlow AI: Turning Messy Thoughts into Clear Tasks with Local AI What I Built I built FriendFlow AI , a privacy-first local AI task organizer for my friend Sandaru , who is a software engineer. Like many developers, Sandaru has a heavy daily workload. He has meetings, development tasks, code reviews, personal errands, reminders, and other responsibilities happening at the same time. The usual solution would be to use a task management application, but I noticed another problem: traditional task managers can actually create more friction for someone who is already busy.

articles.title: Verity Review
articles.excerpt: Verity review: A veritable mess starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson, and Josh Hartnett.
articles.body: Verity is in theaters now. In a Guardian piece on how Colleen Hoover became a global best-selling author, one YA fan that was interviewed by the paper suggested it was because she’s “writing for people who don’t like reading.” If that's the case, then one could argue that the film adaptations of her work are for people who don't like cinema. Now that I've watched all four films inspired by her literary prose — 2024's It Ends with Us, 2025's Regretting You, this year's Reminders of Him, and now Verity — I'm making that case. For these are not adaptations that make any attempt to elevate the middling narratives fumbling around Hoover's novels; I realised this when reading It Ends with Us after suffering through the movie, and I vowed never to read another.

articles.excerpt: Today I learned that one Space Shuttle flight (in 1985) successfully used the Abort-to-Orbit recovery plan (changing its flight path in real time in response to an engine failure during ascent). The o…
articles.body: Today I learned that one Space Shuttle flight (in 1985) successfully used the Abort-to-Orbit recovery plan (changing its flight path in real time in response to an engine failure during ascent). The overall mission continued, accomplished its other objectives, and was considered a success despite the engine failure. articles.title: Dots get up in Muse’s business
articles.excerpt: OpenAI's answer to Muse arrived this week, and it looks a whole lot like Muse dressed up in a suit and tie. Dots is a business-first product - for now, at least - costing a minimum of $100 per month.…
articles.body: OpenAI's answer to Muse arrived this week, and it looks a whole lot like Muse dressed up in a suit and tie. Dots is a business-first product - for now, at least - costing a minimum of $100 per month. And sure, you can make a cute little Dot character, just like you can make a cute little Muse character. But OpenAI's early marketing is all about how you can use it to do Business Things: launch websites, reschedule calls, build slide decks for board meetings. Muse, on the other hand, keeps reminding me to buy a jacket I looked at. This week on The Vergecast , we're talking about Dots and the current state of agentic assistants.
